lines: Inflows to exchanges may precede selling (or collateral…
scenes.sub: Inflows to exchanges may precede selling (or collateral posting, internal moves). Outflows may mean self-custody or DeFi use. Netflow = inflows − outflows. Exchange reserves on-chain aren't proof of solvency (liabilities aren't visible).
scenes.vo: Inflows to exchanges may precede selling (or collateral posting, internal moves). Outflows may mean self-custody or DeFi use. Netflow equals inflows minus outflows. Exchange reserves on-chain aren't proof of solvency (liabilities aren't visible).
scenes.cap: Inflows to exchanges may precede selling (or collateral posting, internal moves). Outflows may mean self-custody or DeFi use. Netflow = inflows − outflows. Exchange reserves on-chain aren't proof of solvency (liabilities aren't visible).

scenes.title: Worked example
steps: One metric is a hypothesis, not a signal.
scenes.vo: Let's work an example, step by step. Netflow +20,000 ETH in a day. Before concluding "selling pressure": check if it's one exchange reshuffling, whether derivatives open interest rose (collateral), and whether price and volume confirm. One metric is a hypothesis, not a signal.

scenes.vo: Question two. Do exchange reserves prove solvency? [[pause 4]] The answer: No. Liabilities aren't visible on-chain.

scenes.q: Is a large inflow always bearish?
scenes.a: No. It can be collateral or an internal move.
